summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of quadriplegia, tracheostomy, GJ tube, and ileostomy was admitted from his nursing home for lethargy and leukocytosis. He was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae, acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration, and hypernatremia. He was treated with IV meropenem and IV fluids, leading to improvement in infection markers and renal function. His supratherapeutic INR led to temporary discontinuation of warfarin. His stage IV sacral ulcer was monitored with no evidence of osteomyelitis, and wound care recommendations were implemented. Iron deficiency anemia was addressed with oral ferrous sulfate, and oral thrush was treated with nystatin and chlorhexidine. He was discharged to extended care to complete his antibiotic course with stable vital signs and resolved symptoms.
